title: Correctness of gate binarization
statement: For every natural number $K$, every gate kind $k$, argument list of length $\ell$, and acyclic existing gate list $gs$ relative to $n$, assume each argument index is less than $n+|gs|$, that $k=\mathrm{NOT}$ implies $\ell=1$, and that $\ell\le K$. Binarizing the gate produces a gate list and output vertex extending $gs$ and forming an acyclic circuit; the output vertex is less than $n$ plus the resulting list length and computes the original gate's value on the values produced by $gs$ for every Boolean input assignment. The resulting list has length at most $|gs|+\ell+2$, its output depth is at most $\lceil\log_2 K\rceil+1$ plus the maximum depth among the argument vertices in $gs$ (with empty maximum $0$), and every added gate is well formed with at most two arguments.
hypotheses_covered: Gate kind $k$ and its argument list, of length $\ell$
Existing gate list $gs$ is acyclic relative to $n$
Every argument index is less than $n+|gs|$
